scenario: AITA for wanting to let my family know my daughter is getting married and post one or two pictures of the cake I'm baking on social media? | My daughter is getting married to her boyfriend of 2 years at the courthouse next week, while he's on leave from the army. This is not a shotgun wedding. They do not plan to have kids for the foreseeable future (if ever.) They intend to have a proper wedding in the future, when finances allow. However, in the meantime, she's forbidden me from mentioning it to anyone in our family or even friends of mine who know her, but do not know the family. These are kids who never had an apartment and want us (the parents) to give them what they need to get started. It's a financial imposition to ask us to furnish their house, and I know that both my family and the groom's family would be delighted to help if they could. In addition, the groom's family all knows this is going to happen and I feel our family will be terribly hurt if they are shut out completely. We're not inviting people to the courthouse, obviously, but they can call and offer their Congratulations anyway. I'm worried that, when they finally do have their wedding, nobody will want to come because they weren't even given the dignity of a notice. Further, I make lots of crafts and baked goods. I like to post the projects on social media for critiques and she's forbidden me from posting the wedding cake picture. Her real wedding will have a professional cake, but I wanted the practice, around just a few of us will be there. Frankly, my enthusiasm for helping her is dwindling and I am contemplating *not* baking the cake, as literally this exposure was all I wanted. I'm also thinking of offering her less for setting up house. My original thinking was, they could save up faster if they don't have to buy furniture and dishes. But she won't let us enlist the help of others. We have to replace what we give her and do without in the meantime, because we don't have money to buy these things right now. We're willing to do this for their comfort. It sure would be nice to see if anyone else is planning on getting rid of some old furniture or dishes so they can get started. Am I being an asshole?

My daughter is getting married to her boyfriend of two years at the courthouse next week. He's on leave from the army, and this isn't a shotgun wedding. They don't plan to have kids for the foreseeable future and intend to have a proper wedding when finances allow. Now, the issue is that my daughter has forbidden me from mentioning the wedding to anyone in our family or even friends who know her but not the family. She also doesn't want me to post pictures of the cake I'm baking for the courthouse ceremony on social media. She's planning to have a professional cake for the future wedding, but I wanted to practice and share the pictures with a few people. I'm feeling hurt because I think our family and the groom's family would be delighted to help if they knew about the wedding. I'm worried that if we don't inform them now, they might feel excluded, and when they finally have the proper wedding, nobody might want to come because they weren't even given the dignity of a notice. Additionally, I make a lot of crafts and baked goods, and I like to post these projects on social media for critiques. My daughter's restriction on posting the wedding cake picture is frustrating because it was a way for me to share my enthusiasm and get feedback. I'm also considering not baking the cake anymore because the exposure was all I wanted, and I'm losing enthusiasm for helping her. She doesn't want us to enlist the help of others, so we have to replace what we give her and do without in the meantime because we don't have the money to buy these things right now. I'm wondering if I'm being an asshole by wanting to inform the family and post the cake pictures, or if my daughter is being unreasonable by restricting me from doing so. First, I need to consider the reasons behind my daughter's restrictions. She might feel that announcing the wedding now would put pressure on the family to contribute financially, especially since they don't have the money to furnish their house. She might also be concerned about privacy or not wanting to draw attention to the courthouse ceremony, which is more of a legal step than a traditional wedding. On the other hand, I feel that our family and the groom's family would want to support them and be part of this important step in their lives. Excluding them might lead to hurt feelings and a lack of support when they finally have the proper wedding. I also need to think about the practical aspects. If I don't inform the family now, will they feel excluded? And if I don't post the cake pictures, am I losing an outlet for my creativity and enthusiasm? Maybe there's a middle ground. Perhaps I can inform the family in a private manner, without making a big announcement on social media. That way, they know about the wedding and can offer their support, but it doesn't put pressure on them to contribute financially. As for the cake pictures, maybe I can share them with a select few close friends or family members instead of posting them publicly. That way, I can still get feedback and share my work without violating my daughter's wishes. I also need to communicate with my daughter about how I'm feeling. She might not realize how hurt I am by her restrictions, and we can find a compromise that respects both our needs. In the end, I don't think I'm being an asshole for wanting to inform the family and share my work. It's important to have open communication and find a balance that works for everyone involved.
